source.creator: 3D Education Engine
source.attribution: Educational model generated procedurally by 3D Education Engine, based on textbook descriptions of mitochondrial structure.

educational.disclaimer: Educational model — not to scale. About 2 µm long; ATP synthase and ribosomes drawn much larger than real.

outer_membrane.name: Outer membrane
outer_membrane.description: Smooth outer boundary; small molecules cross it through channel proteins (porins).

inner_membrane.name: Inner membrane
inner_membrane.description: Holds the electron transport chain; much less permeable than the outer membrane.

cristae.name: Cristae
cristae.description: Folds of the inner membrane that greatly increase its surface area for making ATP.

matrix.name: Matrix
matrix.description: The fluid inside the inner membrane, where the Krebs (citric acid) cycle takes place.

atp_synthase.name: ATP synthase (enlarged)
atp_synthase.description: Enzyme in the inner membrane that makes ATP, driven by hydrogen ions (protons) flowing back through it. Drawn far larger than real.

mtdna.name: Mitochondrial DNA
mtdna.description: Mitochondria carry their own small, circular DNA.

ribosomes.name: Mitochondrial ribosomes (enlarged)
ribosomes.description: Mitochondria have their own ribosomes and make some of their own proteins.
